strings.name: Avi Wigderson
strings.summary: Trained at the Technion and Princeton, Wigderson studies the power and limits of efficient computation. With collaborators, he developed links between randomness, computational hardness and zero-knowledge proofs. He taught at the Hebrew University and the Institute for Advanced Study. He shared the 2021 Abel Prize with László Lovász and was announced in 2024 as the 2023 Turing Award recipient.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced theoretical computer science and randomness research, deepening understanding of computational complexity and the capabilities of mathematical algorithms.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Randomness and computation
strings.highlights.h1.text: With collaborators, studied computational hardness and pseudorandomness, reshaping understanding of randomized algorithms.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: BSc in computer science, Technion (1980); PhD, Princeton (1983).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Shared Abel Prize
strings.highlights.h2.text: Shared the 2021 prize with László Lovász for contributions to theoretical computer science and discrete mathematics.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: Received the 2023 Turing Award, announced in 2024, recognizing research on randomness and computation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Abel Prize
strings.timeline.t2.text: Shared the mathematical award with Lovász for their respective work in theoretical computing and discrete mathematics.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Knuth Prize
strings.timeline.t3.text: Received the Donald E. Knuth Prize for research in theoretical computer science.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joined the Institute for Advanced Study
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became a mathematics faculty member, continuing research connecting complexity, algorithms and mathematics.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Nevanlinna Prize
strings.timeline.t5.text: Received the International Mathematical Union prize for mathematical contributions to information science.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined the Hebrew University
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, later becoming professor and head of its computer science institute.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctoral degree
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed doctoral training at Princeton, studying combinatorial complexity.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Undergraduate degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a Technion computer science degree before pursuing further study in the United States.
